html:
The Whadjuk, shown on the map as Wajuk from 1600 to 1815, are the Noongar people of the country around present-day Perth and Fremantle in Western Australia, along the Swan River.

Their neighbours were other Noongar groups: the Yued to the north, the Ballardong to the east and the Pinjarup to the south. Dutch ships passed this coast in the 1600s, and in 1697 Willem de Vlamingh named the Swan River after its black swans.

In 1829 the British founded the Swan River Colony on Whadjuk land. Settlers fenced the river flats and hunting grounds, and fighting broke out. The Whadjuk warrior Yagan led resistance until he was shot in 1833; his head was sent to England and returned to Western Australia only in 1997. Many Whadjuk died of disease and violence, but their families remain in Perth today.
